title: Nishad Kumar's Double Gold Headlines India's Five-Gold Day at Asian Para Games
excerpt: Kumar cleared a Games-record 2.04m in the high jump T47 a day after winning the long jump, as India's tally at Aichi-Nagoya rose to 35 medals with athletics delivering all five of Tuesday's golds.
body:
• Nishad Kumar won the men's high jump T47 with a Games-record 2.04m on Tuesday, a day after taking the T47 long jump title with 7.11m — becoming only the third Indian to win two golds at a single Asian Para Games.
  • India's para-athletes won five golds on Tuesday, all of them in athletics, as the overall tally climbed to 35 medals — nine gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze — for sixth place at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
  • Deepthi Jeevanji (400m T20, 56.36s) and Simran (200m T12, 24.80s) both defended or set Games records, while Pranav Soorma and Devender Kumar added discus golds.
  • Shooter Manish Narwal's silver in the men's 10m air pistol SH1 also secured India a quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics.

Nishad Kumar cleared 2.04 metres in the men's high jump T47 at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Tuesday to win his second gold medal in two days at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The jump set a new Games record, and it made the two-time Paralympic silver medallist only the third Indian ever to win two gold medals at a single edition of the continental event, according to IANS.

Kumar had opened his campaign on Monday with gold in the men's long jump T47, recording 7.11m twice in the final in an event that remains secondary to his high jump speciality. On Tuesday he was in control from the start of the high jump, passing the first six heights before clearing 1.88m, 1.94m, 1.98m, 2.02m and finally 2.04m, each on his first attempt. The previous Games record of 2.01m had stood to Thailand's Angkarn Chanaboon since Jakarta 2018. Uzbekistan's Muhammadabdulloh Tursunjonov took silver with a personal-best 1.94m, and Chanaboon took bronze with 1.75m.

An elite club of three

Kumar joins runner Ankur Dhama and archer Sheetal Devi, who each won two golds at the Hangzhou edition, as the only Indians with a double-gold Para Asiad. His record in the high jump is deep: silver medals at the Tokyo and Paris Paralympics, gold at the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships in New Delhi — where he set the Asian record of 2.14m — and gold at the previous Asian Para Games in Hangzhou. The world record remains with American Roderick Townsend-Roberts at 2.16m.

Four more athletics golds on a five-gold day

Athletics delivered every Indian gold on Tuesday and 14 medals on the day by the reporting tally, taking the sport's total contribution to 20 of India's 35 medals, The Bridge reported. Deepthi Jeevanji, the 23-year-old from Telangana and a former world champion, defended her women's 400m T20 title in a Games-record 56.36 seconds. Simran won the women's 200m T12 in a Games-record 24.80 seconds despite fatigue she attributed to limited vegetarian food options, and Games debutant Tejalben Damor took bronze in the same race in a personal-best 25.23 seconds.

In the field, Pranav Soorma won the men's discus throw F51/52/53 and Devender Kumar won the men's discus throw F44/64, completing the five-gold athletics haul.

Medals beyond the track

India's day was not limited to athletics. Manish Narwal, a Paris 2024 silver medallist, shot 233.7 to take silver in the men's 10m air pistol SH1 behind South Korea's Jo Jeongdu, a result that also locked in a Los Angeles 2028 Paralympic quota place for India. Debutant Shrishti Arora won bronze in the women's event. In powerlifting, Ashok Kumar Malik upgraded his bronze from the previous edition to silver in the men's 65kg with a best lift of 192kg. Indian swimmers Himanshu Nandal and Niranjan Mukundan added bronzes, and the para table tennis team collected four bronze medals, with Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey becoming India's first podium finishers in the standing category.

Archery and badminton point to more medals ahead. Sheetal Devi, who equalled a world record in the qualification round, reached the women's compound final, and India's doubles pairs advanced to multiple gold-medal matches. In badminton, Pramod Bhagat and Kumar Nitesh assured themselves of medals by reaching the men's singles SL3 semifinals.

What it means

India finished the day sixth in the standings with 35 medals — nine gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze — already a deeper showing across more sports than a single-star campaign. For diaspora readers who followed India's Paris 2024 Paralympic breakthrough, the Aichi-Nagoya results show the bench behind the headline names: debutants on podiums, quota places banked for Los Angeles 2028, and a high jumper who can now win gold in an event that is not even his main one. The Games continue in Aichi-Nagoya this week, with India's archers and badminton players next in line for finals.
